I'm having trouble extracting the SE for density.  I can calculate the SE for density on the link scale from a full-likelihood model using:

sqrt(diag(solve(obj$fit$hessian)))[1]
[1] 0.03377637     # this matches SE.beta for D above

but clearly transforming this to the real scale isn't as simple as it is with the parameter estimates themselves.
exp(-5.055756) yields 0.006372547, the density estimate on the real scale (this also works for the confidence limits), but
exp(0.03377637) yields 1.034353, which is clearly not the SE on the real scale.

Can anyone help me understand how to calculate (or simply extract) the SE on the real scale from a fitted secr model object?

Thanks in advance,
Eric

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: calculate or extract SE of Density from fitted SECR model
parts:
Hi Eric,

The link-scale SE is not typically meaningful on the real scale.  You can back-transform the confidence intervals of course, but in doing so you should notice that they are not symmetrical.  Technically it is possible to approximate an SE on the real scale, but most folks do not bother.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: calculate or extract SE of Density from fitted SECR model
parts:
I don't know about 'most folks', but the delta method SE (for which I presume Eric found the reference in the help) does have its uses as a single-value summary of precision, and as the basis for RSE(D-hat) (or CV(D-hat) as some like to call it). Of course it is a mistake to use +/- 2SE on the 'real' scale as a CI.
Murray
